summary: Judges 21 (25 verses) continues the story of cycle of sin. Starting with 'Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpah, saying, “None of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife.”', it moves through themes of cycle of sin, judge-deliverer and calls readers toward need for king.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows cycle of sin lived out in canaan, cycles of oppression. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpah, saying, “None of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife.”
The whole congregation sent and spoke to the children of Benjamin who were in the rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to them.
In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes.

questions.question: What is happening in Judges 21?
questions.answer: In 25 verses, this chapter judges 21 (25 verses) continues the story of cycle of sin. starting with 'now the men of israel had sworn in mizpah, saying, “none of us will give his daughter to benjamin as a wife.”', it moves through themes of cycle of sin, judge-deliverer and calls readers toward need for king. The setting is canaan, cycles of oppression, written to israel in monarchy. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Judges and why 21 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally anonymous, prophetic history, addressed to israel in monarchy around ~1050 bc events, compiled later. This chapter fits the book's purpose as cycle narrative — its themes of cycle of sin, judge-deliverer build on what came before.

questions.question: Are there any difficult words here?
questions.answer: Scan for names, places, or repeated abstract words like righteousness, covenant, or glory. The glossary below defines up to 3 that show up most. Ask: who is this person, what does this word mean in everyday terms?

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through cycle of sin and judge-deliverer, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 22 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'It shall be, when their fathers or their brothers come to complain to us, that we will say to them, ‘Grant them graciously to us, because we didn’t take for each man his wife in ba...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about cycle of sin. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
